Light blue underneath is your kilowatt consumption — the actual work power your facility uses. That green layer between them? That's reactive kilovolt-amperes reactive — electromagnetic waste that travels back and forth but delivers no productive work. The orange line tracks your power factor hour by hour.

Looking at your production rhythm, I see strong weekday demand blocks running consistently around 800 to 1000 kilowatts consumed throughout the month. Clean weekend valleys drop to baseline levels. You're running about 75 to 80% electric operations — a solid industrial schedule.

But here's the issue — your power factor hovers chronically in the 85 to 92% range with frequent instability. Your reactive demand averages 330 kilovolt-amperes reactive but spikes to 1855 at peak. That reactive burden generates 263,000 BTU per hour of thermal waste, costing you roughly $7 per hour just in additional cooling. Total waste: approximately $182,000 annually.

Now let me show you how we clean this up.

Alright — now we move from observation to correction. Your peak reactive demand hits 1855 kilovolt-amperes reactive. Using our sizing methodology — that's 1855 divided by 400, rounded up — you need five H490 MPTS units for total compensation capacity of 2000 kilovolt-amperes reactive.

The estimated installed investment ranges from approximately $800,000 to about $1.2 million. These are planning-level estimates — final pricing depends on engineering scope, labor requirements, and site-specific conditions.

Here's what MPTS does in plain language. Those five units inject precisely compensating reactive power to neutralize your facility's lagging reactive demand. Power factor rises to 99.5%. The green reactive layer collapses. Your apparent power requirement drops from 787 kilovolt-amperes down to about 681 kilovolt-amperes.

Visually, you'll see the dark blue supply layer pull down much closer to your light blue consumption. Your conductors run cooler. Your transformer thermal burden drops significantly. You free up roughly 100 kilovolt-amperes of capacity headroom.

Now let's move into what you should expect to see. For planning, estimated installed investment is roughly $850,000 to $1,150,000.

PART 3: EXPECTED RESULTS
Now look at the post-MPTS field. This is what harmonized looks like. That green reactive layer has virtually disappeared. Your apparent power tracks much closer to your actual consumption. Power factor holds steady at 99.5% — no more chronic instability.

The numbers tell the recovery story. You're looking at approximately $15,000 monthly in recovered value — that's about $181,000 annually in eliminated waste. With an estimated installed investment of roughly $1 million, you're projecting about a 66-month payback period.

After payback, every hour is recovered value. Your facility draws less current to perform the same productive work. Thermal burden drops by over 260,000 BTU per hour. Cooling costs fall by nearly about $7 hourly. Your transformer operates in a fundamentally cleaner electromagnetic environment.

This isn't just cost reduction — it's capacity liberation. You've freed up substantial electrical headroom for future expansion without upgrading your supply infrastructure.

That's electromagnetic stewardship — and that's the Unity standard.
